source: F1Drive per-car energy-recovery (KERS / ERS) multipliers 2011-2026, researched 2026-10-01 from public sources (Wikipedia car / power-unit / race articles and the motorsport press, every URL per entry). Each number is an ESTIMATE for a game: a documented, ERS-specific statement turned into a score, not a measurement. 2026 = the hand-researched js/cars-data.js values. Summary in Traditional Chinese: docs/ers-data.md.
rules: deploy, harvest, store multiply the ers.power, ers.harvest and ers.store of that season's STANDARD car (1 = standard). They replace the perf.ersPower / perf.ersHarvest multipliers of js/seasons-data.js / js/cars-data.js, they do not stack on them; hasErs false means ers: null for that car. Scale: multiplier = 1 + 0.04 x score. Score 0 = no ERS-specific data (or a neutral documented characteristic); +/-1 a documented edge / small shortfall or a supplier characteristic carried from adjacent seasons (low confidence); +/-2 a clear documented advantage / shortfall; +/-3 a dominant advantage or a serious shortfall (ERS disabled or failing all season); -4..-6 only for the extreme documented harvest deficit (Honda 2015: losing up to 120 kW halfway through a lap). Range enforced: deploy and harvest 0.75..1.15, store 0.9..1.1. deploy: the rules cap the electric power for everybody (KERS 60 kW, MGU-K 120 kW, 2026 350 kW), so deploy stands for how much of that power a car really got on a straight over a season (de-rated or disabled ERS, clipping, failures), not a different hardware rating. harvest: recovery rate (MGU-K under braking; MGU-H 2014-2025). store: 1 everywhere - the usable window is regulated (KERS 400 kJ a lap, 4 MJ 2014-2026) and no exception is documented. hasErs false = the car raced the whole season without KERS (2011: Team Lotus, Virgin, HRT; 2012: HRT, Marussia); its deploy / harvest / store are 1 and ignored. 2010 (out of scope here) is no-KERS for everybody by team agreement. 2013: every car had KERS (Marussia's first, designed by Williams; Caterham with the Red Bull Technologies system). Customers get their supplier's figures (power-unit suppliers must supply an identical specification) unless a team-specific fact is documented: year-old engines (Marussia 2015 with the 2014 Ferrari 059/3, Toro Rosso 2016 with the 2015 060, Sauber 2017 with the 2016 061), Ferrari's 2021 hybrid upgrade documented only for Ferrari's own cars, 2026 works-vs-customer hybrid usage (Mercedes). A single race failure does not change a season figure. 2026: the js/cars-data.js scores (ersHarvest = 1 + 0.01 x report score, ersPower from straight-end telemetry) with their deviation from 1 multiplied by 4, i.e. the same 4 % step as the rest of this file; the Monza 2026 energy-deployment analysis (The Race, 2026-09-05) agrees with the order. note: one line of Traditional Chinese for the car menu, the same for every car of a supplier-season; empty where nothing ERS-specific is sourced. reason: English, the evidence and the score. group: the supplier-season key used to assign the numbers. confidence: high = several consistent ERS-specific sources; medium = one clear ERS-specific source or a well-documented supplier characteristic; low = no ERS-specific data (1.0) or a characteristic carried over / inferred.
